Chapter 1: Zero-Coupling Mandate and Multi-Runtime Parity

Per my last message—and yes, I had to blow Cheeto dust out of my mechanical W switch before typing tthis—most "indie web game devs" on GitHub are straight-up clowns. You clone their repo, run npm install, and watch 400MB of node_modules trash download just to render a laggy 2D square inside a monolithic Game.tsx component where enemy HP, tilemap coordinates, and hitbox offsets are hardcoded inside useEffect hooks. That is suboptimal n00b code. Pure pebkac.

Shadow_Link_Awakening (Sword-Slasher-v2) completely pwns that garbage by enforcing one non-negotiable architectural law from AGENTS.md: the simulation engine must know nothing about the game itself. Source code (.ts, .js, .py) is a pure execution runtime; all game state, physics constants, actor archetypes, level dimensions, sprite sheets, audio synths, and combat tables live exclusively inside decoupled BEJSON 105 (2.0.0-105) files.

1.1 Three Parity Runtimes, One Data Root

Because the data layer is 100% decoupled, Shadow_Link_Awakening runs three independent simulation targets off the exact same game_data/raw/ directory:

  1. **TypeScript / React Client (src/)**:
  • [src/engine/bejsonEngine.ts](https://github.com/boehnenelton/Sword-Slasher-v2/blob/main/src/engine/bejsonEngine.ts) fetches all 24 BEJSON documents from /data/ (public/data/, synced from game_data/raw/) and registers them into bejsonGaming.
  • src/components/GameViewport.tsx renders the 2.5D sorted canvas, HUD, and touch gamepad deck.
  1. **Vanilla ES6 JavaScript Mirror (Engines/JS/)**:
  • Zero framework overhead, zero bundler required. Engines/JS/config.json points raw_data_path to ../../game_data/raw and lib_path to ../../src/lib/lib_js.
  • Engines/JS/main.js loads the exact same .105.bejson and .105a.bejson files via relative URL resolution and runs the same simulation loop.
  1. **Experimental Single-File Compiler (Engines/Experimental/)**:
  • Engines/Experimental/Compiler/Compile.py walks game_data/raw/, packs all 24 datasets into compiled_game_bundle.105.bejson, and injects the entire game into a single offline-runnable standalone-game.html.

Chapter 2: BEJSON 105 (2.0.0-105) MFDB Envelope and Field Map Cache

If you're still storing 500 enemy records as an array of 500 JSON objects repeating "stat_max_health_points_count": 80 five hundred times, congratulations: you're burning RAM and network bandwidth on duplicate key strings. That's legacy garbage.

Shadow_Link_Awakening runs on **BEJSON 105 (Schema_Version: "2.0.0-105")**, a columnar-header + scalar-row matrix format governed by src/lib/lib_bejson_Core_bejson_core.ts. Every table declares Fields once, and Values is a tight 2D matrix of scalar primitives.

2.2 The Field Map Cache & Validation Gate (BejsonCoreEngine)

Look at src/lib/lib_bejson_Core_bejson_core.ts. Positional indexing (row[6]) is strictly banned because inserting or reordering a column would silently corrupt every lookup. Instead, BejsonCoreEngine builds a Map<string, number> once per document:

export class BejsonCoreEngine {
  private fieldMapCache: Map<string, Map<string, number>> = new Map();

  public buildFieldMapCache(docKey: string, fields: BejsonFieldDef[]): Map<string, number> {
    const map = new Map<string, number>();
    fields.forEach((f, idx) => {
      const cleanName = this.sanitizeString(f.name);
      map.set(cleanName, idx);
    });
    this.fieldMapCache.set(docKey, map);
    return map;
  }

  public getFieldValue(docKey: string, row: (string | number | boolean | null)[], fieldName: string): any {
    const map = this.fieldMapCache.get(docKey);
    if (!map) {
      throw new Error(`${E_BEJSON_FIELD_MAP_NOT_BUILT}: Field map cache not found for '${docKey}'`);
    }
    const cleanFieldName = this.sanitizeString(fieldName);
    const colIdx = map.get(cleanFieldName);
    if (colIdx === undefined || colIdx < 0 || colIdx >= row.length) return null;
    const val = row[colIdx];
    return typeof val === 'string' ? this.sanitizeString(val) : val;
  }
}

And before any dataset is trusted, validateDocument(doc) checks:

  1. Format === 'BEJSON' (E_BEJSON_INVALID_FORMAT)
  2. Format_Creator === 'Elton Boehnen' (E_BEJSON_INVALID_CREATOR)
  3. Format_Version in ['104a', '105', '105a', '105db'] (E_BEJSON_UNSUPPORTED_VERSION)
  4. row.length === fields.length for every row (E_BEJSON_RECORD_LENGTH_MISMATCH)
  5. required non-null checks (E_BEJSON_NULL_VIOLATION) and enum membership (E_BEJSON_ENUM_VIOLATION).

No silent undefined leaks, no NaN propagation in physics ticks. If a schema is broken, the barrier catches it at load time.

Chapter 4: 1x Sprite Sheet Slicing and Canvas Pixel Rendering

Let's talk about a classic n00b mistake we caught and nuked during QA: **5-argument ctx.drawImage(img, x, y, 32, 32) on a multi-frame sprite sheet.** If you pass 5 arguments instead of 9 (sx, sy, sw, sh, dx, dy, dw, dh), Canvas squishes the entire 4x4 128x128 sheet (all 16 frames at once!) into a single 32x32 box. Literal clown behavior.

Shadow_Link_Awakening enforces strict 1x-scale sprite sheets in public/assets/sprites/ and public/assets/vfx/, indexed by game_data/raw/sprites/sprites_manifest.105a.bejson and sliced by BEJSONCanvasSpriteManager (src/lib/lib_bejson_Gaming_sprite_canvas.ts & Engines/JS/lib_bejson_Gaming_sprite_canvas.js).

4.1 Crisp Nearest-Neighbor Cell Slicing

Every drawCell call disables bilinear blurring (ctx.imageSmoothingEnabled = false) and computes exact source coordinates (col * frameWidth, row * frameHeight):

public drawCell(
  ctx: CanvasRenderingContext2D,
  sheetKey: string,
  col: number,
  row: number,
  dx: number,
  dy: number,
  dw: number,
  dh: number,
  flipX: boolean = false
): boolean {
  const img = this.images.get(sheetKey);
  const cfg = this.sheets[sheetKey];
  if (!img || !cfg || !img.complete || img.naturalWidth <= 0) return false;

  const sx = col * cfg.frameWidth;
  const sy = row * cfg.frameHeight;

  ctx.save();
  ctx.imageSmoothingEnabled = false;
  ctx.drawImage(img, sx, sy, cfg.frameWidth, cfg.frameHeight, dx, dy, dw, dh);
  ctx.restore();
  return true;
}

Notice the img.complete && img.naturalWidth > 0 guard. If an asset is still streaming over HTTP, the renderer falls back cleanly without throwing InvalidStateError: HTMLImageElement provided is in the 'broken' state.

Chapter 5: 60 Hz Sword Frame Data, Handedness, and Sword Beams

Most browser games treat melee attacks like a single-frame rectangle flash. Shadow_Link_Awakening models real 60 Hz frame data inside Engines/JS/main.js and GameViewport.tsx:

  1. **13-Frame Slash Commitment (~216.7 ms)**: executeSwordSlash() sets slashAnim = { x: px, y: py, dir: playerFacing, timer: 13, maxTimer: 13, variation: varIdx } and swordCooldown = 13. Walking velocity zeroes out during those 13 frames, with zero post-swing recovery lock—you can immediately chain another swing on frame 14.
  2. 4-Frame Phased Swing Visuals: Instead of rendering a static full-arc pie wedge all at once, renderSwordSlash() quantizes progress into 4 discrete frames:
  • Frame 0 (Wind-up): -0.48 * sweepSpan, 0.68x blade reach.
  • Frame 1 (Active Strike): -0.08 * sweepSpan, 1.0x reach + stepped crescent trail.
  • Frame 2 (Peak Cleave): +0.32 * sweepSpan, 1.12x reach + previous-frame ghost afterimage.
  • Frame 3 (Follow-Through): +0.50 * sweepSpan, 0.82x reach, fading trail.
  1. Cardinal Handedness & Mirrored East Arc:
  • Facing UP, DOWN, or LEFT sweeps clockwise (sweepDir = 1).
  • Facing RIGHT mirrors the sweep counterclockwise (sweepDir = -1), matching ambidextrous horizontal sprite mirroring.
  1. **Sword-Hold Stance (isCharging)**:
  • Holding the blade extended locks playerFacing (allowing strafing and backpedaling without rotating), applies a 0.833x (~16.7%) movement speed penalty, and projects an active 20x20 poke hitbox 26px ahead (12 poke damage, 15f recoil, 24f i-frames).
  1. Full-Health Sword Beam:
  • When playerHp >= playerMaxHp, every standard slash spawns a sword_beam projectile (5.5 px/frame, 12 damage) along playerFacing.

const phaseLengths = [0.68, 1.0, 1.12, 0.82];
const sweepDir = facing === 'RIGHT' ? -1 : 1;

Chapter 6: Standard NPC Combat AI and Staggered Frame Rules

Dumb indie games give every enemy if (dist < 200) moveTowardPlayer(). That's baby-mode AI. Shadow_Link_Awakening implements a deterministic Two-Tiered Standard NPC Combat AI in Engines/JS/lib_bejson_Gaming_npc_combat_ai.js (and src/lib/lib_bejson_Gaming_npc_combat_ai.ts) backed by actor_stats.105.bejson.

6.1 Global Status Modes vs. Local Sub-States

  • Global Status Modes intercept normal AI whenever active:
  • STUNNED (stunTimer > 0): Suspends patrol and attack timers while keeping the hurtbox open.
  • HURT / IFRAMES (hurtTime > 0, iframeTime > 0): Applies knockback decay (0.85 friction) and transitions to RETREAT (ranged) or COOLDOWN (melee).
  • Local Behavioral Sub-States: PATROL -> ALERT -> RETREAT / LOCK_ON -> CHARGE / FIRE -> COOLDOWN.

6.2 Staggered 1-in-4 Frame Rule & Linear Search Probes

To keep per-frame CPU flat even with crowded rooms, perception checks run on a staggered 1-in-4 frame cadence:

const evalFrame = ((tickCount ^ slotIndex) & 3) === 0;

Humanoid Hyrule Forces (guard, hyrule_knight, hyrule_archer, hyrule_mage) do not have 360-degree radar. During PATROL, they cast a 176px linear search probe (evaluateLinearSearchProbe) in 16px steps along their current cardinal facing direction, stopping on solid bounds or destructible props. That means Shadow Link can flank behind a patrol without triggering ALERT unless he enters their line of sight, touches them (dist < 26), or hits them.

6.3 Role Differentiation: Shield Knights & Ranged Flankers

  • **hyrule_knight (SHIELD_KNIGHT)**: isFrontalShieldBlock(enemy, playerFacing) checks if Shadow Link's slash or poke hits head-on opposite the knight's facing direction while unstunned. Frontal strikes clang off the kite shield for 0 HP; flanking from the side or rear deals full damage.
  • **hyrule_archer & hyrule_mage (RANGED_FLANKER)**: If Shadow Link closes inside 88px, they transition into RETREAT to re-establish standoff distance, snap to a cardinal firing axis in LOCK_ON, and spawn enemy_arrow (4.4 px/frame) or enemy_bolt (3.6 px/frame).

Chapter 7: Combat Registries, Impact Dynamics, and Cross-Tool Validation

Every serious studio eventually hits a schema drift bug between external asset generators and the runtime engine. Earlier in this repo's lifecycle, Gaming_Editor_Asset_Development emitted 4 combat .105a.bejson tables (shadow_link_combat_animations, weapons_combat_registry, projectile_combat_registry, projectile_impact_dynamics) using Python libraries_105/Lib_PY/Core conventions—implicit column-0 record_uuid (len(row) == len(Fields) + 1) and 2x-scaled PNGs (256x256).

Under Shadow_Link_Awakening's TypeScript bejsonCore.validateDocument, that caused immediate E_BEJSON_RECORD_LENGTH_MISMATCH failures and shifted every Field Map Cache lookup by 1 column. Instead of hacking positional exceptions into the runtime, export_ss2_compatible_pack.py cleanly bridges the two:

  1. Inserts the explicit *_uuid primary key at Fields[0] and *_record_type discriminator at Fields[1].
  2. Upgrades envelope metadata to Schema_Version: "2.0.0-105" with Parent_Hierarchy, Write_Owner_Module, Primary_Key_Field, Type_Discriminator_Field, and Domain_Type_Field.
  3. Downscales 2x PNGs to 1x (128x128, 128x32, 192x192) using Image.Resampling.NEAREST.
  4. Aligns weapon slugs (dark_bow) and audio_manifest.105a.bejson SFX cues (bow_loose, arrow_whistle, flesh_pierce).

Zero runtime hacks, 100% schema parity.

Chapter 8: Zero-Asset Procedural Web Audio Synthesis

Shipping 25MB of uncompressed .wav or .mp3 files for a 2D pixel-art game is pure amateur hour. Shadow_Link_Awakening stores every sound effect and BGM track as mathematical synthesis parameters inside game_data/raw/audio/audio_manifest.105a.bejson.

Each SoundEffectFrequencySpec and AudioAssetManifest row defines:

  • aud_waveform_type: sawtooth, square, triangle, sine, or noise
  • aud_start_freq_hz -> aud_end_freq_hz with aud_frequency_ramp_type (exponential, linear, constant, sequence)
  • aud_duration_ms_metric & aud_default_volume_ratio_metric
  • aud_filter_type (none, bandpass, highpass, lowpass), aud_filter_cutoff_hz, and aud_filter_q_factor
  • aud_note_sequence_json for multi-note chimes (heart_pickup, rupee_pickup, item_chime) and looping boss themes (ganon_theme).

## Chapter 2: BEJSON 105 (`2.0.0-105`) MFDB Envelope and Field Map Cache

If you're still storing 500 enemy records as an array of 500 JSON objects repeating `"stat_max_health_points_count": 80` five hundred times, congratulations: you're burning RAM and network bandwidth on duplicate key strings. That's legacy garbage.

`Shadow_Link_Awakening` runs on **BEJSON 105 (`Schema_Version: "2.0.0-105"`)**, a columnar-header + scalar-row matrix format governed by `src/lib/lib_bejson_Core_bejson_core.ts`. Every table declares `Fields` **once**, and `Values` is a tight 2D matrix of scalar primitives.

### 2.1 Canonical `2.0.0-105` Envelope Contract
Every valid table in `game_data/raw/` enforces these exact top-level metadata keys and `Fields[0]` primary key placement:

```json
{
  "Format": "BEJSON",
  "Format_Version": "105a",
  "Format_Creator": "Elton Boehnen",
  "Schema_Version": "2.0.0-105",
  "Parent_Hierarchy": "../manifest/105a.mfdb.bejson",
  "Write_Owner_Module": "lib_bejson_Gaming_bejson_assets.js",
  "Primary_Key_Field": "spr_uuid",
  "Type_Discriminator_Field": "spr_record_type",
  "Domain_Type_Field": "spr_animation_sheet_type",
  "Records_Type": ["SpriteAssetManifest"],
  "Fields": [
    { "name": "spr_uuid", "type": "string", "required": true, "primary_key": true }
  ],
  "Values": []
}
```

### 2.2 The Field Map Cache & Validation Gate (`BejsonCoreEngine`)
Look at `src/lib/lib_bejson_Core_bejson_core.ts`. Positional indexing (`row[6]`) is strictly banned because inserting or reordering a column would silently corrupt every lookup. Instead, `BejsonCoreEngine` builds a `Map<string, number>` once per document:

```typescript
export class BejsonCoreEngine {
  private fieldMapCache: Map<string, Map<string, number>> = new Map();

  public buildFieldMapCache(docKey: string, fields: BejsonFieldDef[]): Map<string, number> {
    const map = new Map<string, number>();
    fields.forEach((f, idx) => {
      const cleanName = this.sanitizeString(f.name);
      map.set(cleanName, idx);
    });
    this.fieldMapCache.set(docKey, map);
    return map;
  }

  public getFieldValue(docKey: string, row: (string | number | boolean | null)[], fieldName: string): any {
    const map = this.fieldMapCache.get(docKey);
    if (!map) {
      throw new Error(`${E_BEJSON_FIELD_MAP_NOT_BUILT}: Field map cache not found for '${docKey}'`);
    }
    const cleanFieldName = this.sanitizeString(fieldName);
    const colIdx = map.get(cleanFieldName);
    if (colIdx === undefined || colIdx < 0 || colIdx >= row.length) return null;
    const val = row[colIdx];
    return typeof val === 'string' ? this.sanitizeString(val) : val;
  }
}
```

And before any dataset is trusted, `validateDocument(doc)` checks:
1. `Format === 'BEJSON'` (`E_BEJSON_INVALID_FORMAT`)
2. `Format_Creator === 'Elton Boehnen'` (`E_BEJSON_INVALID_CREATOR`)
3. `Format_Version` in `['104a', '105', '105a', '105db']` (`E_BEJSON_UNSUPPORTED_VERSION`)
4. `row.length === fields.length` for every row (`E_BEJSON_RECORD_LENGTH_MISMATCH`)
5. `required` non-null checks (`E_BEJSON_NULL_VIOLATION`) and `enum` membership (`E_BEJSON_ENUM_VIOLATION`).

No silent `undefined` leaks, no `NaN` propagation in physics ticks. If a schema is broken, the barrier catches it at load time.

### 4.1 Crisp Nearest-Neighbor Cell Slicing
Every `drawCell` call disables bilinear blurring (`ctx.imageSmoothingEnabled = false`) and computes exact source coordinates `(col * frameWidth, row * frameHeight)`:

```typescript
public drawCell(
  ctx: CanvasRenderingContext2D,
  sheetKey: string,
  col: number,
  row: number,
  dx: number,
  dy: number,
  dw: number,
  dh: number,
  flipX: boolean = false
): boolean {
  const img = this.images.get(sheetKey);
  const cfg = this.sheets[sheetKey];
  if (!img || !cfg || !img.complete || img.naturalWidth <= 0) return false;

  const sx = col * cfg.frameWidth;
  const sy = row * cfg.frameHeight;

  ctx.save();
  ctx.imageSmoothingEnabled = false;
  ctx.drawImage(img, sx, sy, cfg.frameWidth, cfg.frameHeight, dx, dy, dw, dh);
  ctx.restore();
  return true;
}
```

Notice the `img.complete && img.naturalWidth > 0` guard. If an asset is still streaming over HTTP, the renderer falls back cleanly without throwing `InvalidStateError: HTMLImageElement provided is in the 'broken' state`.

## Chapter 5: 60 Hz Sword Frame Data, Handedness, and Sword Beams

Most browser games treat melee attacks like a single-frame rectangle flash. `Shadow_Link_Awakening` models real 60 Hz frame data inside `Engines/JS/main.js` and `GameViewport.tsx`:

1. **13-Frame Slash Commitment (`~216.7 ms`)**: `executeSwordSlash()` sets `slashAnim = { x: px, y: py, dir: playerFacing, timer: 13, maxTimer: 13, variation: varIdx }` and `swordCooldown = 13`. Walking velocity zeroes out during those 13 frames, with **zero post-swing recovery lock**—you can immediately chain another swing on frame 14.
2. **4-Frame Phased Swing Visuals**: Instead of rendering a static full-arc pie wedge all at once, `renderSwordSlash()` quantizes progress into 4 discrete frames:
   - `Frame 0` (Wind-up): `-0.48 * sweepSpan`, `0.68x` blade reach.
   - `Frame 1` (Active Strike): `-0.08 * sweepSpan`, `1.0x` reach + stepped crescent trail.
   - `Frame 2` (Peak Cleave): `+0.32 * sweepSpan`, `1.12x` reach + previous-frame ghost afterimage.
   - `Frame 3` (Follow-Through): `+0.50 * sweepSpan`, `0.82x` reach, fading trail.
3. **Cardinal Handedness & Mirrored East Arc**:
   - Facing `UP`, `DOWN`, or `LEFT` sweeps **clockwise** (`sweepDir = 1`).
   - Facing `RIGHT` mirrors the sweep **counterclockwise** (`sweepDir = -1`), matching ambidextrous horizontal sprite mirroring.
4. **Sword-Hold Stance (`isCharging`)**:
   - Holding the blade extended locks `playerFacing` (allowing strafing and backpedaling without rotating), applies a `0.833x` (`~16.7%`) movement speed penalty, and projects an active `20x20` poke hitbox `26px` ahead (`12` poke damage, `15f` recoil, `24f` i-frames).
5. **Full-Health Sword Beam**:
   - When `playerHp >= playerMaxHp`, every standard slash spawns a `sword_beam` projectile (`5.5 px/frame`, `12` damage) along `playerFacing`.

## Chapter 6: Standard NPC Combat AI and Staggered Frame Rules

Dumb indie games give every enemy `if (dist < 200) moveTowardPlayer()`. That's baby-mode AI. `Shadow_Link_Awakening` implements a deterministic **Two-Tiered Standard NPC Combat AI** in `Engines/JS/lib_bejson_Gaming_npc_combat_ai.js` (and `src/lib/lib_bejson_Gaming_npc_combat_ai.ts`) backed by `actor_stats.105.bejson`.

### 6.1 Global Status Modes vs. Local Sub-States
- **Global Status Modes** intercept normal AI whenever active:
  - `STUNNED` (`stunTimer > 0`): Suspends patrol and attack timers while keeping the hurtbox open.
  - `HURT` / `IFRAMES` (`hurtTime > 0`, `iframeTime > 0`): Applies knockback decay (`0.85` friction) and transitions to `RETREAT` (ranged) or `COOLDOWN` (melee).
- **Local Behavioral Sub-States**: `PATROL -> ALERT -> RETREAT / LOCK_ON -> CHARGE / FIRE -> COOLDOWN`.

### 6.2 Staggered 1-in-4 Frame Rule & Linear Search Probes
To keep per-frame CPU flat even with crowded rooms, perception checks run on a staggered 1-in-4 frame cadence:

```javascript
const evalFrame = ((tickCount ^ slotIndex) & 3) === 0;
```

Humanoid Hyrule Forces (`guard`, `hyrule_knight`, `hyrule_archer`, `hyrule_mage`) do **not** have 360-degree radar. During `PATROL`, they cast a `176px` **linear search probe** (`evaluateLinearSearchProbe`) in `16px` steps along their current cardinal `facing` direction, stopping on solid bounds or destructible props. That means Shadow Link can flank behind a patrol without triggering `ALERT` unless he enters their line of sight, touches them (`dist < 26`), or hits them.

### 6.3 Role Differentiation: Shield Knights & Ranged Flankers
- **`hyrule_knight` (`SHIELD_KNIGHT`)**: `isFrontalShieldBlock(enemy, playerFacing)` checks if Shadow Link's slash or poke hits head-on opposite the knight's `facing` direction while unstunned. Frontal strikes clang off the kite shield for `0` HP; flanking from the side or rear deals full damage.
- **`hyrule_archer` & `hyrule_mage` (`RANGED_FLANKER`)**: If Shadow Link closes inside `88px`, they transition into `RETREAT` to re-establish standoff distance, snap to a cardinal firing axis in `LOCK_ON`, and spawn `enemy_arrow` (`4.4 px/frame`) or `enemy_bolt` (`3.6 px/frame`).
